meta.name: Track Stripe cancellations and classify churn reasons with Claude and Gmail

name: Ask why customers cancelled in Stripe and categorise the answer

parameters.content:
## Ask why on every cancellation, and keep the answer

Cancellations are the one moment a customer will tell you the truth, and almost nobody asks. This fires on the Stripe cancellation, asks one question, sorts the answer into a category you can count, and tells you when the reply is worth a human response.

### How it works
Two triggers sit in one workflow. The Stripe trigger fires on a cancelled subscription, looks up the customer for their email, and reads Stripe's own cancellation details, because someone who cancelled through the billing portal has often already given a reason. When they have, no survey is sent. When they have not, they get one short email with a single question and a link to the form. The form trigger catches the reply and builds the same record, so both paths meet at one place. One AI call sorts it into a fixed set of categories, decides whether it was preventable and whether a reply is worth trying, and writes one next step. You get an email flagged by urgency, and a row lands in your churn sheet so the categories add up over time.

### Setup
- Edit the config node: brand, sender name, who to notify.
- Open the Form Trigger, copy its production URL and paste it into the config so the email can link to it.
- Add credentials: Stripe, Anthropic on the analysis node, Gmail, and Google Sheets pointed at your churn log.

### Customization
Route save-worth-trying replies to Slack, add a discount offer to the ask email, or branch on account value so only larger accounts get a personal follow-up.

Built by **nocode.expert**, done-for-you automation and AI workflows. https://nocode.expert/resources/churn-exit-survey-automation

## 1. Catch the cancellation
Stripe often already holds a reason when the customer cancelled through the billing portal. If it does, do not send a survey asking again.

## 2. Ask once, briefly
One question, one click, no login. The email says the cancellation is already done, so it does not read as a retention trap.

## 3. Sort the answer
A fixed set of categories so the numbers add up over months. The model never infers a reason nobody gave.

## 4. Flag what is worth a reply
Most cancellations need no response. The email leads with whether this one does.
